newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Lukoil plans over $1 bln in global issue next year.
newsitem.headline: Lukoil plans over $1 bln in global issue next year.

text.p: Russia's biggest oil company OAO Neftyanaya Kompaniya LUKoil plans to raise at least $1 billion through a global placement of its shares next year, Vice-President Leonid Fedun said on Monday.
"The main task on the capital market next year is a global placement of more than 100 million shares," he told a news conference.
"Given current prices we expect that would exceed $1 billion."
Other issues and placements would raise $300 million, Fedun said.
Fedun said LUKoil had virtually completed preparations for a London stock exchange share placement likely to take place in March or April.
"We will place our ADRs and convertible bonds there," he said.
LUKoil was one of the first Russian companies to issue level-one American Depositary Receipts and has also already issued convertible bonds.
It plans to issue level-one ADRs on its preferred shares after the New Year holidays, he said.
By the end of 1997 it intends to issue level-three ADRs, which unlike level-one receipts raise new capital, on its ordinary stock.
It plans a formal application for the issue at the end of the second quarter of next year, and the process generally takes three or four months, Fedun said.
The issue would depend on market conditions and the attitude of the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, he said.
International accountancy firm KPMG has already prepared an audit to U.S. GAAP standards of LUKoil's 1994 accounts, and 1995 accounts would be ready by March next year.
By March 1997 LUKoil would also apply for credit ratings from two leading international rating agencies, he said.
Other projects under consideration are an issue on foreign markets of unsecured short-term bonds, and longer-term secured bonds running for JL PTH
Helped by its ADR issue, LUKoil is one of the most popular Russian companies with foreign investors and its shares are considered one of the blue chips on the Russian market.
Company officials have emphasised that a global share offering, probably through the New York Stock Exchange, will take priority over a Eurobond issue.
LUKoil is one of only a few Russian oil companies whose output is increasing.
Earlier on Monday it said production of crude oil in the first nine months of this year was 1.18 million barrels per day, up from 1.16 million in the same 1995 period.
Net profit rose 118 percent to 2.61 trillion roubles on sales of 32.56 trillion, up 137 percent, according to Russian accounting standards.
At 1410 GMT LUKoil was $11.30 after closing at $11.20 on Friday. Preferred shares were not traded on Monday, but finished on Friday at $8.23.
